question: Why is Obscura 0.2.5 lighter than us on the same 25-pool crawl (199 MB vs 297 MB peak RSS)?
relationship_verdict: NOT a fork. Obscura is its own codebase (obscura-* crate family on deno_core 0.350 -> v8 137.3.0). diting cites obscura#NNN issues as ported fixes (the 'steal mechanisms not protocol' doctrine, #276); the engines share no code lineage. We retired deno_core (own diting_runtime + snapshot container), they still ride it.

facts.isolation_model: BOTH isolate-per-page (ours: Vm::from_snapshot per navigation; theirs: deno_core JsRuntime::new per page) — the shape is the same

snapshot_blob_bytes.note: ours is 2.75x — the 300015 fingerprint surface (17k-line bootstrap, 701-name global_surface, canvas face, interface sweep) bakes a much larger object graph

measurement_per_isolate_aginxbrowser.method: release binary, 25 sessions each navigating a trivial data: URL (near-zero page content), ps RSS on the server pid
measurement_per_isolate_aginxbrowser.reading: ~7.4 MB per empty-page realm. 25 concurrent = ~185 MB of pure JS-realm baseline; the 4.6 MB snapshot deserialized per isolate is the dominant term. Crawl peak 297 MB = base 25 + 25x7.4 + DOM/layout/net per page. Closing sessions returns only part (209 -> 151 MB; V8 page retention).

obscura_arithmetic: same multiplier (25 targets = 25 JsRuntimes), smaller per-unit: ~1.68 MB snapshot + deno_core 0.350 / V8 137 baseline. 199 MB observed is consistent with per-isolate in the ~3-4 MB class. Not directly measured (no CDP driver at hand) — hedged.
tradeoff_and_options: The fat snapshot IS the 300015 armor (xhs shield reads the window surface; the 701 names exist because walls checked for them). Slimming it trades fingerprint coverage for memory.
Two-tier snapshot: slim core baked, surface expansion applied post-restore only on fingerprint-sensitive hosts (needs a lazy-expansion mechanism; ~ms per flagged page).

Realm recycling per session (reuse isolate across navigations) would cut concurrent isolates but breaks the fresh-realm-per-page hygiene that the current model (and the busy_frozen/rebuild semantics) is built on — not recommended casually.
Heap knobs (--max-semi-space-size etc.) do NOT touch the snapshot baseline — the 2026-10-22 v8flags experiment already showed ~no peak movement.
Idle shrink: after-close retention (209->151 MB) suggests a MemoryReducer/background-reclaim pass could return tens of MB on session churn.

followup_2026_10_25_heap_decomposition.probe: AGINXBROWSER_REALM_HEAP_STATS (now a shipped forensics knob): Vm::heap_statistics at [A post-restore]/[B post-init], Vm::drop and Page::drop counts, actor-task end

fingerprint_surface_share.method: throwaway build with global_surface.js+canvas_face.js skipped from SNAPSHOT_SCRIPTS
fingerprint_surface_share.verdict: LAZY-SURFACE REJECTED: the P2/P3 surface is 0.83MB/realm (16% of the 5.2MB heap) — max 21MB over 25 realms, not worth descriptor-fidelity risk. The snapshot mass is the ENGINE'S OWN JS standard library (17k-line bootstrap + family), i.e. capability, not decoration.

followup_2026_10_25_heap_decomposition.close_path_verdict: CLEAN — 25/25 actor tasks ended, 25/25 diting Pages dropped, 51/51 Vms dropped; SerializedDropRuntime and malloc_zone_pressure_relief both work. (An earlier 'zero drops at close' reading was an artifact of benching a stale server instance on the same port.)

post_close_residual.immediate: RSS ~151MB (vs 25MB base) — looks like a leak, is not
post_close_residual.cause: V8 memory pool (flag --memory-pool, default on) retains freed isolate heap pages for --memory-pool-timeout=8s to make isolate churn fast, then releases automatically
post_close_residual.deployment_knob: AGINXBROWSER_V8_FLAGS=--no-memory-pool trades churn speed for immediate return (existing engine knob; no code change needed)

remaining_honest_levers: committed-vs-used slack ~1.1MB/realm (6.6 total vs 5.5 used) — heap growing-factor experiments could trim ~25MB at 25-realm peak
per-realm cost is dominated by the engine's JS stdlib mass; per-context-in-shared-isolate would slash it but is the rejected isolation-model change

shrink_batch_2026_10_25.tier_dial_verdict: gzip-style time dial at INIT is DEAD: critical memory pressure + double full GC (tier -9, ~5ms) recovers only 33KB more than one low_memory_notification (tier -1, ~2ms) — the live object set (5.07MB) is the floor; physical after tier-1 (5.18MB) already sits 0.11MB above it.

idle_shrink.design: session actor's pump arm: after 5 consecutive quiet 200ms slices (~1s parked), full-GC the realm; any command resets the clock. Same AGINXBROWSER_REALM_SHRINK knob, now DEFAULT ON (user call: 2ms is free).
idle_shrink.demo: single session on a data: page churning ~5MB garbage per 160ms for 10s, then parked. knob OFF: RSS climbs to 105MB and STICKS at 105MB for 15+ s of idle. knob ON (default): churn peak ~68MB, within ~1s of idle RSS drops to 47MB and stays — ~58MB reclaimed per parked garbage-heavy session, permanently.
idle_shrink.init_shrink_unchanged: 2.07ms per realm build, physical 6.62->5.18MB per realm, 25-realm peak 210.8->194.8MB (-7.6%)

crawl_scale_trap_and_gate.ungated_default_on: Amiibo crawl 940/940: wall 62.2s, CPU 22.7s, peak 270MB — vs shrink-off (34.4s / 15.0s / 297MB): the 2ms single-session cost becomes ~8ms CPU per navigation under 25-way concurrency (lock contention), +7.7s CPU amplified to +28s wall for −27MB. CPU delta is engine-side proof, network-independent.
crawl_scale_trap_and_gate.gate: init shrink now runs only when live isolates <= 8 (diting_runtime::live_isolates); idle shrink (the parked-session 105→47MB win) stays unconditional — it provably never fires during crawl-style command churn.
crawl_scale_trap_and_gate.gated_verification: Amiibo crawl 940/940: CPU 17.5s (back at the 15s baseline class; extra wall 54.9s is tonight's network — CPU is the engine-side signal), peak 300MB (no shrink tax). Single-session garbage demo still lands 46MB flat after idle.
